title: Media language & representation
examples: How does a magazine show what it means to be healthy?
Can you give me an example of a stereotype in advertising?
What is the difference between a sign and a stereotype?

explain.say: Today we are looking at how media presents ideas to us.

items: Media shows us ideas through language.
We look for signs and patterns.

explain.say: A sign is something that stands for something else.

draw.text: Sign: Something that stands for something else

explain.say: Stereotypes are oversimplified ideas about groups of people.
Representation is how a person or group is shown in media.
Think about advertisements for cleaning products.
A common mistake is assuming a single image is always true.

draw.text: Mistake: Assuming one image is always true

faq.q: What is the difference between a sign and a stereotype?
faq.a: A sign is a specific symbol that points to something, while a stereotype is a broad, often inaccurate generalization about an entire group of people.

faq.q: How do I spot a stereotype in a film?
faq.a: Look closely at the characters shown; are they all behaving the same way regardless of their background?
asks: Are there signs of bias in media?

faq.q: Does representation always mean showing the truth?
faq.a: No, representation is just how something is shown, and that can be selective or misleading.
asks: Is representation the same as reality?

faq.a: Yes, many signs, like hand gestures, have different meanings depending on the culture you are in.

faq.q: Why do media companies use stereotypes?
faq.a: They sometimes use them because they are familiar and easy for a wide audience to understand quickly.
asks: Why is it easy to use stereotypes?

facts: Signs can be visual, auditory, or textual.
Stereotypes reduce complex identities to simple, often inaccurate, traits.
Representation involves the choices made about what to include or leave out.
Media language uses codes and conventions to communicate meaning.

quiz.say: A cartoon character always shown as clumsy and unintelligent is an example of:
quiz.why: This is a generalization about a group, not a specific symbol.

wrong.0: A sign is a specific symbol, like a stop sign.
wrong.1: Representation is the overall way the character is shown, but the specific idea is a stereotype.
wrong.2: A code is a system of signs, but the generalization itself is the stereotype.

quiz.say: The use of bright, primary colours in a commercial is an example of:
quiz.why: The colour itself is a visual sign that communicates energy or fun.

wrong.0: Language is too broad; the colour is a specific, contained sign.
wrong.2: A stereotype relates to people groups, not just colours.
wrong.3: Representation is the whole picture; the colour is just one element or sign.

quiz.say: When a news report only features one type of expert opinion, this limits the:
quiz.why: This describes the overall way the topic is shown, limiting viewpoints.

wrong.1: A sign is a single element, not the limitation of many viewpoints.
wrong.2: While it might create a stereotype, the core issue is the lack of varied showing.
wrong.3: A code is a system; the issue here is the imbalance of voices.
